nodes.label: Data model overview: text = block tree in CRDT (Yjs; Yrs on iOS), handwriting layer of vector strokes with anchors, encrypted attachments, metadata; all formats versioned from day one (R-03)
Stroke anchor types: text range, paragraph (margins), drawing block, image
Server responsibilities: accounts, storing and relaying encrypted changes, attachments, realtime, API and MCP, handwriting PNG rendering for agents

Server components: app server Node.js + TypeScript (Fastify); PostgreSQL via Drizzle (accounts, notebooks, rights, tokens, encrypted updates, snapshots, agent log; pg-boss queue); file storage on disk by default, S3-compatible optional
No Redis (D-25): single process, realtime broadcast in memory behind an interface (PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY or Redis/Valkey later)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the stack small while allowing scaling without touching other code

nodes.label: No MinIO (D-26): file storage behind interface with «disk» and «S3» implementations
Server address in clients (D-49): «Сервер» field at login/signup, default ours, own https server checked via GET /v1/health; address stored with account; web uses own domain

iOS build 17: «Сервер» field above email, scheme optional (https added), http only for localhost; Return/«Войти» checks GET /v1/health and shows «name · version» before password is sent; no field when DS_SERVER_URL empty
Share and invite links carry the server address
Several servers/accounts at once — stage 6
Self-hosting: whole server via docker compose up (infra/): server + PostgreSQL; VPS 2 cores, 2–4 GB; ~300–400 MB idle
Daily backups of DB and files stored outside the VPS; restore verified (R-11)
Server implementation rules (apps/server, infra/; ПРЕДЛОЖЕНО, revised via coordinator)
Server stores Argon2id(loginKey) and Argon2id(recoveryLoginKey), m=19 MiB t=2
nodes.rationale: Keys are already high-entropy; the client did the heavy Argon2id

nodes.label: prelogin for unknown email returns deterministic fake salt (HMAC of server secret); login/recovery for unknown email take equal time
Device = session: JWT access token 15 min with userId + deviceId; revocation immediate (checked on every request, WebSocket closed)
Refresh token 30 days, single-use; reuse = theft → device revoked; repeat within 60 s (REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE_SEC) returns same new token (HMAC-derived, not stored); clients refresh sequentially

Recovery key replacement POST /v1/auth/recovery-key (password-confirmed): old key stops at once, pending recoveries cancelled; password change, recovery, key change logged (GET /v1/me/security-events)
Password change revokes all other devices; recovery by recovery key revokes all (new session issued)
Session also contains deviceId; optional deviceName in signup and recovery/finish

Per-account storage quota USER_STORAGE_QUOTA_BYTES (default 10 GB, D-53; 0 = unlimited): updates, snapshots, attachments; guest/agent writes count to note owner; counter users.storage_bytes kept by DB triggers; over quota → payload_too_large; 10% snapshot headroom
Signup DS_SIGNUP=open (default, D-53) | closed | invite (DS_INVITE_CODES); retry of same signup after lost response works in any mode
Any signup conflict (email, userId, accountDocId taken) → same 409; email enumeration contained by rate limits
nodes.rationale: Without email confirmation the refusal itself reveals a taken address

nodes.label: seq assigned in a transaction under document row lock — strictly increasing without gaps; live updates delivered in seq order
Repeated push with same clientMsgId from same device → ack with previous seq, no duplicate
deviceId in updates: user device from access token; guest:<22-char hash of shareId and hello deviceId>; agent:<grantId>
Sync errors: invalid message → bad_request (ref = clientMsgId); protocol_mismatch only for unsupported version; deletion → doc_not_found with ref = docId

Sync limits: update 2 MB, snapshot 16 MB (was 50 MB, lowered by audit 2026-10-27), awareness 64 KB, 100 msg/s per connection (burst ×5, checked before JSON parse; rate_limited with retryAfterMs); awareness only for subscribed docs

Before hello frames ≤64 KB (else close 1009); ≤30 connections per IP and 10 per account (guests per link): rate_limited retryAfterMs 30000 + close 1013 (SYNC_MAX_CONN_PER_IP, SYNC_MAX_CONN_PER_USER); socket reading paused at 32 queued messages until 8
subscribe: duplicates collapsed (last since wins); duplicates or >1000 docs per message (MAX_SUBSCRIBE_DOCS) → bad_request; batch output ≤8 MB; docs with >1 MB after snapshot paged (audit 2026-10-27)
Snapshots made by client (>500 updates or >1 MB) and on leaving a document after ≥30 edits (ПРЕДЛОЖЕНО web-app); server snapshots agent-mode notebooks itself after agent edits
History versions = snapshots (GET /v1/docs/:id/versions)
Retention: updates covered by latest snapshot kept 7 days; snapshots — latest always, all for 7 days, daily to 30 days, weekly to a year, then monthly (HISTORY_*)
Batched first sync: 200 docs per query when ≤100 updates after since/snapshot; backpressure while >4 MB unread in socket; 10 000 notes ~1.2 s server-side (target spec/11 «up to a minute»)
subscribe with since < latest snapshot seq always gets snapshot + tail, even if intermediate updates are still stored (sync-protocol §5, 2026-10-26)
nodes.rationale: A device unable to read some updates (wrong key from a client bug) recovers from a later healthy snapshot

nodes.label: Notebook share grants access to notebook index and all its notes, incl. ones created later

Guest token lives as long as the link; revoking link disconnects guests at once; at link expiry open guest connections closed (unauthorized «share expired», code 4401); guests may read and (with edit) upload attachments, not delete
Deleting a note or notebook revokes its links
Agent layer = @datascratch/agents package (stream agents); server provides grant/OAuth/log storage, document decryption and user login (apps/server/README.md)

Each agent data request runs in a transaction under PostgreSQL role ds_agent with Row-Level Security per grant: only its agent-mode notebooks, writes only with read_write; revoked/expired grant sees nothing; notebook key decrypted only inside
nodes.rationale: Even a buggy query cannot read or write someone else's notebook

nodes.label: Notebook switched to private → agents lose access immediately; deleted notebook removed from grants
Agent image attachment decrypted only up to 20 MB (AGENT_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES); access checked inside ds_agent transaction, reading/decryption after it without holding a pool connection (audit 2026-10-27)
OAuth consent screen opens in browser; web app sets session cookie via POST /v1/auth/web-session

pg-boss background jobs: doc-compact (after new snapshot), cleanup (hourly: deleted attachment files, abandoned uploads >7 days, expired tokens, revoked devices >30 days), history-sweep (daily retention)
GET /metrics (Prometheus) enabled by METRICS_TOKEN, requires Bearer token: HTTP, sync messages/errors, stored updates (user/guest/agent), connections, PG pool, memory; no route without token
Logs hold no user data: error fields whitelisted, DB query parameters (emails, hashes, ciphertext) and PostgreSQL detail dropped from message and stack (audit 2026-10-27)

X-Forwarded-For accepted only from private-network proxies (TRUST_PROXY default loopback,linklocal,uniquelocal); client address = rightmost entry added by untrusted hop; nginx fragment passes $remote_addr only
Per-email rate limit: 10 attempts/min per request kind for login, signup, prelogin, recovery, across IPs; exceeded → 429 rate_limited (was 500)
Any invalid message before successful hello closes the connection (code 4400)
Uploading a chunk of an attachment deleted mid-write → 404, written file moved to storage_trash

PATCH /v1/docs/:id { notebookId } moves note between notebooks: history, attachments, note key unchanged (client rewraps key); old-notebook share guests lose note, note share stays; agent access recomputed by RLS

POST /v1/fetch-image { url } (D-52) with SSRF protection: http/https ports 80/443, no credentials; every resolved IP must be public (IPv6 only global 2000::/3, embedded IPv4 forms rejected, tricky IP notations normalized); connect to verified IP; ≤3 redirects rechecked; no cookies/Referer; ≤20 MB, 15 s; only image/* with verified signature (no SVG); 60/min per account, 2 concurrent per account, 4 per server; URL not logged (ds_fetch_image_total)

Automatic deploy workflow (infra/DEPLOY.md): GHCR images of server and web (+Caddy), SSH to user VPS (DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_SSH_KEY), idempotent prep, migrations → compose up → HTTPS checks (API, web, WebSocket, /metrics closed) → rollback on failure; sslip.io domain fallback
No Docker Hub on server (often unreachable from Russia): Docker from Ubuntu repo, all images incl. PostgreSQL in GHCR
Memory budget VPS 2 CPU / 4 GB: PostgreSQL 1 GB (shared_buffers 256 MB), server 1 GB, Caddy 256 MB; shared server 512/512/128 MB
Inspect mode: read-only reconnaissance before deploy (system, memory, disk, ports, Docker, web servers, firewall) without secrets, no DEPLOY_ENABLED needed
Deploy guard DEPLOY_ENABLED=true; on shared server nothing foreign changed (existing Docker, ufw, auto-updates untouched; own compose project datascratch)
Coexistence with Sinhron: own site file in /etc/sinhron/caddy-sites/, shared docker network edge, caddy validate before reload, own file removed on error

If 80/443 busy: listen only on 127.0.0.1:8480 behind existing proxy; ready nginx/Caddy/Traefik fragments; optional DS_NGINX_AUTO=true with backup, nginx -t, rollback; DEPLOY_MODE standalone | behind-proxy
Trash: trashedAt encrypted in notebook index (server cannot see it); after 30 days client calls DELETE /v1/docs/:id; server deletes doc, history and attachments at once
Attachments: separate encrypted files, loaded on demand, resumable upload
Handwriting rendered to PNG for agents (server)
